text:
Many people are paid earlier in December, before the holidays, but January's pay comes at the normal time. If your December pay lands on 15 December and January's on 29 January, that's 45 days on one pay: six and a half weeks instead of four. Standard Bank has called it the 49-day pay gap: for people normally paid at month-end, it can be as long as 49 days. And January isn't cheap: rent on the first, debit orders, and in 2027 public schools open on 13 January, with uniforms, shoes and stationery to buy. In Debt Rescue's survey, more than a third of people said back-to-school costs were their biggest worry in January.

Full guide: "Festive Season on a Budget: How Not to Start January Broke (South Africa 2026)" on the Money From Zero channel.
